# Managed Postgres pricing, normalized

If the database can sleep, Neon Free is $0 (1 GB storage, 100 CU-hours, scale-to-zero after 5 minutes). For a small always-on database, Crunchy Bridge Hobby-0 is $9/month plus $0.10/GB storage, DigitalOcean's 1 GiB / 10 GiB plan is $15.15/month, and AWS db.t4g.micro is $11.68/month of compute in us-east-1 Single-AZ (storage unverified from the HTML page). Self-hosting on a Hetzner CX23 is $6.49/month if you will operate Postgres. Railway has no published Postgres SKU — it uses the same CPU, RAM, and volume rates as apps.

Prices from each provider's official pricing page, checked 17 Oct 2026. USD, excluding tax. Always-on hours use 730 h unless a vendor publishes a 30-day month (Fly MPG storage). "Not published" or "unverified" means the page did not list that number. Estimates, not guarantees. AWS RDS storage (gp3 $/GB-month) was not in the fetched HTML — omitted rather than guessed.

PostgreSQL Hosting Options in 2026: Pricing Comparison | Bytebase

# PostgreSQL Hosting Options in 2026: Pricing Comparison

Adela · Oct 12, 2026

Update history

1. Oct 12, 2026 Prisma Postgres: Free plan storage is now 1.01 GB (was 500 MB).
2. Oct 2, 2026 AWS Aurora: Serverless v2 scales to zero (0 ACU minimum), per-ACU-hour rates, Aurora PostgreSQL in the AWS Free Tier, express configuration.
3. Sep 29, 2026 Prisma Postgres: free tier now 200k operations, operations count any Postgres client, plans include Prisma Compute app hosting.
4. Jul 12, 2026 Add Prisma Postgres; Neon's post-Databricks usage-based pricing; PlanetScale current tiers; Timescale renamed TigerData; fix Heroku free-tier error.
5. Apr 1, 2026 Add PlanetScale Postgres.
6. May 6, 2025 Initial version.

This post is maintained by Bytebase, an open-source database governance platform that can manage PostgreSQL hosted in any providers. We update the post every year.

PostgreSQL remains the default choice for relational databases in 2026. This article compares hosting from the major clouds (AWS, GCP, Azure) and specialized providers (DigitalOcean, Aiven, Neon, PlanetScale, Prisma, Supabase, TigerData, Heroku), focusing on pricing models and key cost factors.

## Understanding Pricing Models#

Three pricing models dominate:

Instance-Based: Pay hourly for fixed vCPU/RAM; storage and I/O billed separately. Common with major clouds.

Usage-Based/Serverless: Pay only for what you use — compute, storage, I/O, and data transfer. Ideal for variable workloads.

Tiered Plans: Fixed-price bundles from specialized providers offer predictable costs but less flexibility.

# Simple, predictable pricing

Always know what you'll pay with monthly caps and flat pricing.

## Managed Databases

Fully managed MongoDB, Kafka, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Caching database engines to give your application the performance it needs-without the operational overhead of managing your own database server.

Learn more about DigitalOcean's Managed Databases or talk to an expert.

### PostgreSQL Standard

PostgreSQL is an open source, object-relational database built with a focus on extensibility, data integrity, and speed. Its concurrency support makes it fully ACID compliant, and it supports dynamic loading and catalog-driven operations to let users customize its data types, functions, and more.

Choose Advanced Edition for high-concurrency or data-intensive workloads requiring maximum throughput, rapid failover, self-serve controls, and deep observability.
